correctness.rationale: Threshold-two tests depend only on caps at two, and capped addition respects merging into destination colours. Each occupied initial part–colour class moves as a unit; tagging one vertex from each class preserves its labelled trajectory, even when two actual class sizes share a cap. All labelled colours return exactly when all tags return, giving the max entry time and lcm period. An independent bounded reconstruction checked all 17,576 nonempty profiles and 109,512 occupied tags, found max entry nine and periods {1,3,4,6,12}, and verified T^21=T^9 on every tag. It found recurrent profile counts 174, 1826, 18, 6 and 126 in that order, and separately reproduced the K_{5,3,2} time-nine witness by direct labelled updates. The exceptional profiles yield 2, 1 and 7 symmetry classes; per chosen large shore period four has 6 orientations with 2×2 small-shore labellings, period six has 6 orientations with 2³ labellings, and per chosen small shore period twelve has 18,18,6 orientations with 1,2,6 labellings at sizes 1,2,3. Each specified two-large-colour shore has B(n)=2^n−2n−2 assignments. These give the claimed R formulas (states, not cycles), while multinomial weights of all profiles give the transient/period census. Independent replay: /workspace/branches/401e679c-cf1e-4b34-b176-a4f92f9a5b3d/independent_check.py and independent_output.log. The frozen checker sources and output are supporting evidence; small labelled examples alone do not prove the all-size result.

evidence: Each recurrent capped profile is a member of a computed quotient cycle: the return permutation in the earlier comparison code guarantees physical recurrence and gives the same p for any realization of its caps. Sum the independent per-shore multinomial weights over the profiles of each such p, with each profile counted once. For the exceptional patterns, one/two/three singleton occupied colours and two specified large colour classes yield factorial weights and the binomial-sum factor B(n).

For all initial profiles, using the same lifted_trace already supplied, first entry is the first t≤9 for which the occupied traces agree at t and t+12; the identity at times 9 and 21 and the period set justify the test. The period is the least divisor of 12 returning all occupied buckets at time 9. Applying the same multinomial weights gives D_{t,p} directly, although the matching entry explicitly does not tabulate labelled basins.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Thus failure is not a claim that the published comparison prints the same R or D formulas. They are obtained from its exact finite quotient data and elementary labelling multiplicities, rather than a new mathematical classification of orbits or basins.

evidence: 51f1d9876496 reports 826 quotient cycles with counts 174,614,9,2,27 by labelled period. These are counts of quotient cycles, not labelled configurations. Its code enumerates the actual profile cycles and computes len(cyc) times the permutation order to label each cycle, before reducing to minimum-size and freedom-flag existence patterns.
80bbc6695856 gives a related census on K_{a,b,c} but uses Greenberg–Hastings: both refractory colours advance automatically. Its period spectrum, sharp transient and R12 coefficients differ.
exact_database_or_table.reasoning: Do not equate the raw quotient counts with R_p. The profile-level certificate for precisely the same rule contains the needed inputs to recover R_p, unlike the Greenberg–Hastings tables.

originality.rationale: A distinct indexed result has the identical update, graph family, sharp identity and entry bound, exceptional period spectrum and three phase regimes, plus a period-three existence criterion. The same result supplies the exact recurrent capped profiles via its executable cycle enumeration and computes the labelled least period on each capped cycle. The frozen explicit labelled multiplicities are not printed there, but they are a mechanical multinomial weighting of those profiles; the transient census likewise weights profiles after a finite comparison of the supplied bucket traces. The strongest overlap was indexed later; this comparison concerns scientific coverage and mechanical implication, not who discovered it first or whether the records are independent. No distinct surviving dynamical or non-mechanical counting claim is established here.
residual_risks: Indexed dates do not settle priority or relationship between the two same-rule records.
Application of the older finite-network theorems could not be settled from their accessible material.

value.rationale: On a natural dense graph family, the sharp uniform cutoff, exceptional primitive-period regimes, and all-size counts separate genuine vertex-level waves from artefacts of merging or capping. In particular the eight six-cycles isolated on K_{2,2,2} illustrate why physical period rather than population period is meaningful. The intrinsic usefulness of this classification is distinct from the finding that a matching catalogue already provides the dynamics and a sufficient certificate to recover the counts.
